summary: Granular smoothing flag suppressed hourly buffer credit across DST boundary for Dedicated account
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a missing hourly buffer credit (warmup/free buffer) for a Dedicated account after a weekend run spanning the DST hour boundary. Impact: Boxwell observed ~5-7% higher invoice line for dedicated hours for 2024-11-03 23:00–2024-11-04 02:00 US/Eastern. They expect buffer credits to offset microburst warmups; credits are absent for the hour containing the DST fallback.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer ran scheduled micro-batch warmup jobs on dedicated pool (tagged 'prod:boxwell') spanning 2024-11-03 23:30 - 2024-11-04 01:30 US/Eastern.
2) Postback system attributes hourly buffer credits based on 'hourly-window' tags and smoothing flags.
3) System evaluated smoothing policy with 'granular_rate_smoothing' feature flag enabled; credits generated for neighboring hours but not the DST fallback hour.
4) Customer compared Console estimate (shows buffer applied) vs finalized provisional invoice (shows no buffer line for that hour).
Expected: Hourly buffer credit applied for all covered hours; Actual: Missing credit for DST fallback hour (clock moved back one hour).

investigation_notes: 2024-11-12 09:14 - Support: Confirmed customer cohort uses Dedicated reserved pool and consistent tagging. Console estimate showed buffer; provisional invoice lacked it.
2024-11-12 11:02 - Billing eng (Daniel P): Replayed postbacks for the hour and saw postbacks processed but buffer allocator flagged window-length-mismatch when 'granular_rate_smoothing' was on.
2024-11-12 14:40 - Metering service logs show event counts consistent across windows; the allocator uses epoch-based hour boundaries which did not normalize the repeated hour during DST fallback.
Hypothesis: The granular smoothing allocator's window normalization assumes monotonic hourly windows and rejects duplicated clock hours, causing credits to be suppressed for the repeated hour.

Risk: Affects accounts with scheduled jobs spanning DST fallbacks and any region with manual clock adjustments or similar repeated-hour artifacts. Could under-apply buffer credits and increase customer invoices by a small percentage for affected windows.

Mitigation considered: patch metering window normalization to canonical UTC hour buckets before smoothing evaluation; backfill allocator to re-evaluate affected postbacks for 24h window; issue a provisional credit if validated.
Related: INT-40122 flagged a similar allocator assumption during scheduled maintenance; PR referenced for discussion is meter fix PR #3312.
